description: Fail-closed production inventory for GC graph and Runtime-root mutations used by incremental collection.

mutation_context.sweep_policy: A checked managed-object write during Sweep abandons the remaining cursor. Propagate/Atomic writes re-trace black owners; a changed cross-StateArena edge abandons Propagate.
mutation_context.allocation_policy: Objects allocated during an active cycle are black and publish their complete initial object graph. Thread/Upvalue allocation conservatively restarts because lua_core cannot enqueue StateHandles.

families.mechanism: Every post-publication write uses GarbageCollector::with_mut; the post-write barrier re-scans the complete Table under its current weak mode.
Live Function writes use GarbageCollector::with_mut. Direct add_upvalue calls in PublicationTxn occur before the Function allocation is registered.
Compiler Proto mutation is confined to an unpublished Rust value; active-cycle create publishes its complete initial graph before returning.
Closed-value and close transitions use GarbageCollector::with_mut. A changed StateHandle edge restarts Propagate; Atomic closure re-traces the resulting Value.
Live metatable writes use GarbageCollector::with_mut. Typed payload mutation is non-GC data and is not an object edge.

production_locations.symbol: coroutine publication and activation link maintenance

families.mechanism: Runtime Thread writes use PublicationTxn::with_mut or GarbageCollector::with_mut. Changed StateHandle edges restart Propagate; caller edges use the normal owner scan.

State writes occur only during scheduler turns. Root snapshots cover logical top plus every active CallInfo register window and re-scan all known reachable states at Atomic. Allocation-triggered cycles run to completion at one safe point; explicit bounded cycles retain the audited Atomic rescan contract.
The safe-point driver seeds global/registry/fixed roots, native activation buffers, and temporary State roots at cycle start and Atomic.
